before.evidence:
COMPARISON:Plain films [Date].

CLINICAL HISTORY:Twisting injury 4 weeks prior. Suspected transient lateral patellar dislocation.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the left knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The medial meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament and posterior oblique ligament are intact. The fibular collateral ligament is intact. Biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. The iliotibial band is intact. Popliteus tendon insertion is intact.

No femoral trochlear dysplasia. No patellofemoral subluxation. The TT-TG distance measures 20 mm, above the upper limit of normal. The patellar retinacula are intact. Once again seen are well-corticated osseous fragments at the tibial tuberosity in keeping with chronic sequelae of remote prior Osgood-Schlatter's disease. Minimal marrow edema and tiny cysts are noted in the fragments. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Full-thickness cartilage denuding patellar apex and along the lateral patellar facet. Mild lateral femorotibial chondrosis. Preserved medial femorotibial articular cartilage.

Trace knee joint fluid. Small Baker's cyst. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Lateralization of the tibial tubercle, predisposing to patellofemoral maltracking/instability. No patellofemoral subluxation.
2. High-grade patellofemoral chondrosis suggesting evolving moderate patellofemoral osteoarthritis of the left knee.
3. Chronic sequelae of remote prior Osgood-Schlatter's disease, also shown previously.
4. Mild lateral femorotibial chondrosis.

after.evidence: Full-thickness cartilage denuding patellar apex and along the lateral patellar facet.

As described above Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

None

before.evidence:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: 64-year-old with progressive left knee pain related to "wear and tear". Evaluate for cartilage loss. Evaluate for meniscus tear.
Comparison: No recent left lower extremity imaging available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee is acquired in 3 anatomic planes at 1.2 Tesla using a local extremity receiver coil and a noncontrast protocol.

FINDINGS:

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Osseous and articular alignment at the left knee are normal.
No fracture. No focal osseous contusion.
No evidence for a recent pivot shift mechanism.

JOINT SPACE:
There is a small left knee effusion.
There is a minimal, partially ruptured Baker's cyst.
No intra-articular bodies.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is a complex tear of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn with a dominant oblique undersurface component and a smaller inner margin radial component at the junction posterior horn and posterior root. There is moderate subsequent medial meniscus extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: There is diffuse partial-thickness cartilage loss all along the weightbearing region of the medial femoral condyle, with focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the medial femoral margin.
There is partial-thickness cartilage loss at the medial tibial margin.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: The lateral meniscus shows normal morphology and signal with no tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage throughout the lateral tibiofemoral compartment is normal.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
There is a small region of focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the patellar median ridge, with more diffuse partial-thickness cartilage loss extending along the medial patellar facet.
There is diffuse partial-thickness cartilage loss with deep chondral fissuring at the central femoral trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal morphology and signal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): The MCL is bowed from medial meniscus extrusion, but intact.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: The fibular-collateral ligament and anterolateral ligament are normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Intact stabilizers.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Moderate degenerative hypertrophic distal quadriceps tendinopathy, with intrasubstance degeneration at its patellar attachment and mild enthesopathy. No high-grade quadriceps tear.
Patella tendon: Normal morphology and signal with no tear or degeneration.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No significant soft tissue edema in Hoffa's fat.
A TT-TG distance is normal at 7 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
The distal iliotibial band and biceps femoris are normal.
The distal semimembranosus is normal.

SOFT TISSUES:
Neurovascular structures in the popliteal fossa are normal.
Subcutaneous soft tissues are normal. No soft tissue mass.

IMPRESSION:

1. Extensive complex medial meniscus tear with a dominant oblique undersurface component at its body and posterior horn, moderate medial meniscus extrusion, and high-grade cartilage loss on the medial femoral condyle with low-grade cartilage loss at the medial tibial margin.

2. Focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the patellar median ridge with high-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss at the central femoral trochlea.

3. Moderate degenerative hypertrophic distal quadriceps tendinopathy, with mild enthesopathy.

4. Small left knee effusion with a minimal ruptured Baker's cyst.
